race.name: GFNY Ottawa
race.tagline: A fully closed 118-kilometer race where Kanata rollers, technical turns, and crosswinds make a flat profile tactically expensive.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing on fully closed roads
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Four official aid stations on the long route
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules

climate.primary: Early-fall wind on exposed rural roads
climate.description: The official course description warns that proximity to the river makes crosswinds likely. Riders move quickly from an urban opening to wooded rural roads, so exposure and temperature can change across the lap.

terrain.surface: Paved urban and rural roads around the Kanata North tech hub, fully closed to vehicle traffic for the race.
features: A flat, fast opening with sharp technical turns
Seven kilometers of false flat on Marchurst Road
A three-kilometer rise gaining 50 meters at up to 4.5 percent
A second long-course lap after roughly 60 kilometers

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Canada's first GFNY pairs a credible fully closed course with championship positioning and strong city access. Inaugural execution and modest climbing cap the score.

climb_profile.king_of_mountain: There is no major mountain; the selection comes from repeated false flats, crosswinds, and the second lap's accumulated speed.

course_description.character: Ottawa's long race covers 118.3 kilometers and 784 meters of climbing on a fully closed course. The route mixes technical early turns, long false-flat roads, a short northern climb, and two laps, making group economy and repeatable power more important than pure climbing speed.
course_description.signature_challenge: Beginning the second lap after roughly 60 kilometers without having overspent on the fast first circuit.

logistics.airport: Ottawa International Airport (YOW) is the primary gateway for the host city.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Kanata near the Richcraft Recreation Complex or along a direct route to the race hub.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, road closures, parking, and start access.
logistics.food: Kanata and central Ottawa have abundant restaurants and groceries; practice taking fuel while riding in a fast group before race week.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced its first Canadian race in April 2026, using a fully closed course based at the Richcraft Recreation Complex in Kanata.
notable_moments: 2026: GFNY announces its first race in Canada
history.reputation: A high-potential inaugural race with unusually strong road closure support but no execution history yet.

biased_opinion.summary: Ottawa looks easy if you read only the elevation total. That misses the point. The combination of full road closure, technical turns, false flats, crosswinds, and a second lap encourages speed that can turn small positioning mistakes into a very long chase.
weaknesses: Wind can dominate the race character
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Race Ottawa if you want a fast, tactical fondo where efficiency and position matter every bit as much as watts per kilogram.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fully closed 118-kilometer race where Kanata rollers, technical turns, and crosswinds make a flat profile tactically expensive.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race Ottawa if you want a fast, tactical fondo where efficiency and position matter every bit as much as watts per kilogram.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Pittsburgh for more climbing, or GFNY Maryland Cambridge for a longer established Mid-Atlantic race.
